title: A review's done --dry-run writes no gone evidence that its --commit run then leaves uncommitted
goal: bl_land.rerun_done_checks records a gone check in its item's evidence only on a run that commits (never under done --dry-run), so done SP-review --dry-run followed by done --commit leaves a clean tree; the stale-docs branch's commit_written also runs only after the dry-run return. A planted test, named done_dry_run_gone, runs done --dry-run then done --commit on a review with a gone check and asserts a clean tree after the second. Found by the SP-evkj4avq review in _tools/bl_land.py rerun_done_checks (called before the dry-run return).

gates.question: How does a review's done keep a dry run from leaving gone-check evidence an uncommitted --commit run then misses?
options: record gone checks only on a run that commits, never under --dry-run
done --commit commits every item file whose evidence a dry run already wrote
gates.recommendation: record gone checks only on a run that commits, never under --dry-run
gates.answer: record gone checks only on a run that commits, never under --dry-run

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-10 whole-backlog triage, which the operator asked to end with every draft planned into a sprint or dropped (sprint 10 of 13, "backlog.py fixes: land, drop, precheck and usage text"); it blocks no fitness test and no real user reported it, so it sits in a late sprint of the sequence.
